messages:
Jeff: Quick sync — I want to formalize the "rollback runway" concept for canary/A-B so we don't flip on short-lived noise.
Owen: clarify: are we talking ingestion lag, probe propagation, or transient infra noise?
Maria: all of the above. + KV-cache warmups and cold-shard p99 spikes. those are real and common.
Tina: billing/cost signals show up late too; we can't base instant rollbacks on them alone.
Jeff: proposal: a sliding runway of windows (e.g., 5 windows of 60s). assign exponentially decaying weights favoring recent windows. require weighted composite > threshold for K consecutive windows to trigger.
Owen: sensible. but per-route SLOs differ: how to make this configurable?
Maria: rollout-level policy config. defaults for most routes, overrides for critical low-latency ones. surface in console.
Tina: interface boundary: orchestrator emits candidate decisions to a decision bus. local agents maintain authority to act immediately for severe local signals. avoid sync orchestrator -> router RPC in critical path.
Jeff: yes: async pub/sub, local reconcile. local agent can short-circuit when it sees severe symptoms (e.g., doubled p99 + error spike), then report and let central analyze.
Owen: what metrics feed the composite score?
Maria: p50/p95/p99 deltas, error-rate change, generation-quality regressions (sampled evals), and token-cost delta. also sample counts and ingestion lag for confidence.
Tina: normalization is key. per-metric rolling baseline -> compute z-scores, clamp, then weight. prevents scale mismatches.
Jeff: example rollback config snippet for discussion:
```
rollback_policy:
  runway_seconds: 300
  windows: 5
  required_consecutive_windows: 3
  composite_threshold: 2.1
  metric_weights: {p99:0.45, errors:0.35, cost:0.15, quality:0.05}
  post_rollback_cooldown_minutes: 30
```
Owen: who computes composite: local or central?
Maria: hybrid: local computes lightweight realtime composite (latency+errors). central computes heavyweight composite with quality and billing. central can veto, contextualize, and set confidence.
Tina: central veto must not block critical local fallbacks. local should be able to act first; central may request rollforward only with high-confidence signals and operator approval.
Jeff: we need hysteresis: after automated rollback, block auto-rollouts for that route for cooldown and require manual approval to re-deploy same variant.
Owen: telemetry fields to include in decision trace: metric z-scores, sample counts, ingestion timestamps, baseline mean/std, composite value, and signal entropy.
Maria: central analyzer will also publish a confidence score (function of sample count and ingest lag). low confidence => downgrade to alert instead of auto-rollback.
Tina: ops: every decision must be auditable. record which metrics tripped, weights, timestamps, and raw samples. keep traces for 7 days by default and surface a one-line rationale in console.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled local aggregate job created — emits rollup every 30s to the decision bus.
Jeff: decision bus message shape should include rollout_id, route, variant_id, composite_score, contributing_metrics, sample_counts, and confidence.
Owen: add an action_id in the message so operators can acknowledge/annotate the automated decision.
Maria: for quality signals, central will run periodic sampled-eval jobs and attach a diff histogram; include example failures for triage.
Tina: RFC items: message schema, local agent authority matrix, cooldown semantics, and UX for trace display in console.
Jeff: action items:
- Owen: prototype local scoring lib + config parsing (owner: Owen)
- Maria: produce normalization notebook + threshold guidance (owner: Maria)
- Tina: draft RFC for decision bus + message schema (owner: Tina)
- Infra: wire up 30s local aggregates and test ingest lag (owner: infra)
Jeff: target: end-of-week spike-resistant prototype for internal playtest. keep automated actions reversible and auditable.
Owen: opening a draft PR today.
Maria: will share notebook link once ready.
Tina: starting RFC now, will link PRs.
Jeff: thanks. final note: surface the decision trace prominently so ops can quickly see "why" and revert if needed.
Owen: 👍
